q: What metering and calibration rules apply to a CCTS offset project's monitoring plan?
title: CCTS offset metering and calibration rules
short: Readings that change all the time, such as fuel used or power generated, must be measured continuously. Fixed values like emission factors are updated at least once a year. Meters must meet BIS, national or IEC standards and be calibrated by an NABL accredited lab, and data is kept for two years after the last issuance.
audience: Plant engineers and consultants writing a CCTS monitoring plan

sections.h: The requirements in the project standard
ul: Continuously varying data (fuel inputs, heat or electricity produced, gas captured): measured continuously and recorded at set intervals.
Generally constant data (emission factors, calorific values, efficiencies): taken from published sources at least once a year, unless the methodology asks for more.
Measuring equipment certified to BIS, national or IEC standards.
Calibration by an NABL accredited organisation.
Uncertain readings cross-checked against other data sources.
Methods, accuracy, intervals, responsible people and QA/QC procedures written into the plan.

p: All monitored data is archived electronically for two years after the crediting period or the last issuance of credits, whichever is later.
Fuel supplier invoices and electricity bills are the usual cross-check for meter readings, and BEE's fossil fuel tool prefers calorific values printed by the supplier on the invoice.

senseible: Senseible keeps fuel and electricity invoices as dated, fingerprinted monthly records, the consumption data a project's monitoring report and its verifier will ask to trace.

sources.label: BEE, Detailed Procedure for Offset Mechanism under CCTS, Version 1.0 (effective 27 March 2025)
